Plotting basics with rvisPlot

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

rvisPlot() dispatches a chart request to a wrapper function. Set type to the chart method and plotter to the wrapper prefix, then pass the data and the dimension mappings that the chart needs.

species <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, FUN = mean)

rvisPlot(
  type = "bar",
  plotter = "amCharts",
  obj = species,
  x = "Species",
  y = "Petal.Length",
  config = list(title = "Mean petal length by species")
)

The same input and dimension mappings can be sent to other wrappers that implement bar, such as billboarder, c3, googleVis, highcharter, or plotly. Each wrapper has its own configuration options and may impose additional data requirements. The chart type manual lists the exact wrapper methods and their arguments.

Examples of every chart type with each of its plotters are in the chart guides: comparing categories, parts of a whole, relationships and distributions, time series, networks and hierarchies and tables.

Dimension arguments

Dimension arguments such as x, y, label, and theta refer to columns in obj. Use a character column name for a single field. Use a named list when the wrapper supports multiple series and the series need distinct names, for example y = list(actual = "actual", forecast = "forecast").

series <- data.frame(
  date = as.POSIXct("2025-01-01", tz = "UTC") + (0:11) * 86400,
  actual = 30 + sin((0:11) * pi / 6) * 5,
  forecast = 31 + sin((0:11) * pi / 6) * 4
)

rvisPlot(
  type = "tsline",
  plotter = "amCharts",
  obj = series,
  x = "date",
  y = list(actual = "actual", forecast = "forecast"),
  config = list(title = "Actual and forecast")
)

Configuration

Supply wrapper settings through config, a named list. Common settings include titles, axes, legends, colors, and layout options. Configuration keys are wrapper-specific: consult the configuration reference for the accepted type, default, and valid values of every key recorded by the package. Extra ... arguments are forwarded to the underlying chart constructor where the wrapper supports them.

Choosing a wrapper

The wrappers are optional dependencies. Install the plotting package for the wrapper you plan to use. Then change plotter while keeping the chart type, data, and mappings when both wrappers implement the same chart. The package’s chart type index shows which exact methods are available.
